title: Korea Close | November 27, 2026
desc: Foreign buying of 1.13 trillion won and hopes for a market stabilization fund lifted the KOSPI 4.34 percent to 4,915.68 as the KOSDAQ jumped 8.13 percent and the won firmed to 1,337.9 per dollar.
html:
Foreign investors bought more than 1 trillion won of KOSPI shares on hopes that a government market stabilization fund would start buying, and the index jumped 4.34 percent. Bond yields rose with stocks, and the won posted its strongest 3:30 p.m. close since November 20.

On Friday, November 27, 2026, the KOSPI opened 0.37 percent higher, stayed near flat in early trade, then pushed through 4,800 and 4,900 to close at 4,915.68, its first finish above 4,900 in three sessions. The KOSDAQ did better still, rising 8.13 percent and tripping a buy-side sidecar. Yonhap and Newspim both pointed to the same catalyst: regulators have called two meetings for November 29 and 30 on the market stabilization fund.

The close

KTB 3-year 3.685 percent, up 6.3 basis points. KTB 10-year 3.832 percent, up 4.2 basis points. Both come from Yonhap's closing bond table, published at 4:42 p.m. KST, and match the Bank of Korea's ECOS daily figures.

USD/KRW 1,337.9 at the 15:30 Seoul close, down 4.8 won from the previous session's 1,342.7.

KOSPI 4,915.68, up 204.47 points, or 4.34 percent.

KOSDAQ 708.99, up 53.28 points, or 8.13 percent.

KRX cash market, KOSPI: foreigners net bought about 1.13 trillion won and institutions about 239 billion won, while individuals net sold about 1.77 trillion won, per Yonhap's KRX closing table. Other outlet tallies differ slightly. None of these figures include NextTrade.

What changed

The Financial Services Commission has scheduled a meeting of the fund's investment management committee for Sunday, November 29, and an emergency market stability meeting with the heads of the five largest financial groups and Korea Development Bank for Monday, November 30, Financial News reported. The fund was set up in 2020 at 10.76 trillion won and has never put money into the market. Officials are checking whether lenders can commit more.

Foreign investors led the buying. Their 1.13 trillion won net purchase was the largest since September 7, according to Yonhap, and pension funds added 288.3 billion won. Samsung Electronics rose 4.55 percent to 179,100 won and SK hynix gained 5.41 percent to 1,110,000 won. Brokerages led all sectors with an 11.43 percent gain. Mirae Asset Securities jumped 15.87 percent. Bank stocks slipped, with Shinhan Financial down 0.94 percent.

Samsung Electronics also paid a dividend of about 30 trillion won, or 4,601 won a share, the largest payout by a Korean company, Financial News reported. Yonhap noted some hope that reinvested dividends would support demand for shares.

The KOSDAQ sidecar hit at 10:22 a.m. KST, with KOSDAQ 150 futures up 6.06 percent, per Newspim. It was the index's biggest percentage gain since July 31 and its first close above 700 since November 11. Gainers beat decliners 1,559 to 142. Jusung Engineering rose 14.36 percent and Rainbow Robotics 13.70 percent.

Bonds sold off as stocks rallied, extending the move that followed the Bank of Korea's hawkish dot plot on November 26. The 2-year closed at 3.716 percent, above the 3-year. The 30-year fell 2.7 basis points to 3.900 percent. Yonhap Infomax linked that long-end strength to a December issuance plan that trims competitive auctions to 2.2 trillion won.

In currencies, the dollar rose to 1,347.1 won in the morning, then gave way to foreign stock buying and month-end exporter selling, Yonhap reported. Dollar demand from foreign shareholders sending Samsung dividends home cushioned the fall.

Where the signal stops

KOSPI regular-session trading value came to 12.86 trillion won, a moderate number for a 4 percent day. Gainers led decliners 783 to 109, according to Yonhap, but individuals used the rally to sell 1.77 trillion won. Food and telecom stocks fell. Han Ji-young of Kiwoom Securities told Yonhap the rebound could stay limited until fresh money actually reaches the market.

RYZM's reading: The session priced in a fund that has not yet bought a single share, so the November 29 and 30 meetings now carry real weight. Foreign and pension money did show up. Individual selling hints that local retail did not trust the bounce. Yields rising alongside stocks suggests bond traders are still working off the Bank of Korea's dots, not a growth scare.

Next

November 27: U.S. stock markets close early at 1 p.m. ET, which is 3 a.m. KST on November 28.

November 29: The stabilization fund's investment management committee meets.

November 30: Financial Services Commission Chairman Lee Eog-weon chairs an emergency market stability meeting with financial industry heads.

December 1, 11:00 a.m. KST: Korea's November trade data, per a market calendar listing.

December 2: Korea's November consumer price index, per the national statistics agency's release schedule.

December 3: Nvidia's Jensen Huang is scheduled to appear at a U.S. Senate hearing, Yonhap reported.
